_note: 6E Standard (400) archetype characteristics. AUTHORED, not lifted — there is no legacy 6E prose.
Why authored: 6E figures nothing. In 5E, PD/ED/SPD/REC/END/STUN fall out of STR/CON/DEX for free,
and OCV/DCV come off DEX. In 6E every one of those is bought, and OCV/DCV/OMCV/DMCV are sold
outright at 5 points per +1 over a base of 3. A 5E spread dropped into 6E is a hero with PD 2 and
Benchmarked against the five real 400-point 6E characters in the fixture corpus — identified by
spending ~400 and taking exactly 75 in complications, which is the 6E Standard limit:
chars powers skills | STR DEX CON INT EGO PRE OCV DCV OMCV DMCV SPD  PD  ED REC END BODY STUN
So the shape of a real 400-point hero is roughly chars ~170 / skills ~55 / powers ~170, with the
Brick trading powers away for characteristics (254/69/63). These spreads keep each archetype's 5E
identity — the Gadgeteer's INT, the Mentalist's EGO, the Brick's STR — at 6E's conventions.
No cost is declared anywhere. The engine prices every spread (see characteristicsBudget), and the
powers budget is whatever is left of the 400.
Spelling: 'archetypes', not the legacy file's 'archtypes' typo. This file is new, not lifted.

archetypes.name: Energy Projector
archetypes._note: starborne is the model: a ranged blaster. High OCV to land the blast, DEX and END to keep throwing it.

archetypes.name: Gadgeteer
archetypes._note: The INT of the set — the gadgets are powers, so the body behind them is ordinary. But not *that* ordinary: SPD 4 and DCV 6 put it at -10.7% of the Rule of X with a powerset already dead on the baseline, and no real 400-point character in the corpus runs below SPD 5. SPD carries weight 20, the heaviest in the model — it is not flavour.

archetypes.name: Martial Artist
archetypes._note: jane-fawn is the model: OCV 9 and SPD 6, and famously no bought defences — the skill IS the defence.

archetypes.name: Mentalist
archetypes._note: greyman is the model: the mental combat values are the whole point, and 6E is the edition that finally sells them separately. OCV stays low. SPD 5 because nothing at this tier is slower — greyman himself is a SPD 5 mentalist.

archetypes.name: Metamorph
archetypes._note: All-rounder — the shapes are powers, so the base body is solid rather than specialised. PRE carries the 5E identity.

archetypes.name: Mystic
archetypes._note: EGO and END feed the magic; ED over PD, because what a mystic soaks is rarely a fist. Mental defence bought, mental offence left to powers. SPD 5 — see the Gadgeteer's note.

archetypes.name: Patriot
archetypes._note: The super-soldier: good at everything, best at nothing. The 5E spread already spent the most here (125 of 250) and this keeps that shape.

archetypes.name: Powered Armor
archetypes._note: The suit is powers; INT drives it and the defences are the pilot's own. Slightly tougher than the blaster, slightly slower.

archetypes.name: Speedster
archetypes._note: DEX and SPD are the identity, and DCV is where the speed shows in combat. 6E decouples CV from DEX, so the DCV here is a deliberate buy rather than a side effect.

archetypes.name: Weapons Master
archetypes._note: The weapon is a power; the aim is a characteristic. OCV over DCV — this one hits rather than dodges.

archetypes.name: Brick
archetypes._note: jack-diamond is the model, and the one archetype that buys its powerset away: STR, PD and STUN eat the budget, and what is left over is small on purpose. That is what a Brick is.
